newsitem.title: USA: Gambling Ohio editor given probation.
newsitem.headline: Gambling Ohio editor given probation.

text.p: The editor of a weekly newspaper who admitted stealing $10,000 from his paper's Christmas fund to support an addiction to scratch-off lottery tickets was sentenced on Thursday to five years probation.

Hamilton County Common Pleas Court Judge Melba Marsh spared the editor, Les Wilson, a jail sentence because she said she was moved by letters of support. Wilson, 73, admitted the theft in a January column and quit the Valley Courier newspaper, saying he hoped to be sent to prison for life.
"I lost more than money. I ruined my life," Wilson said in court. "If what is happening to me can keep one or two people from getting in this same condition I will be happy."

Wilson, who is recovering from a fractured hip suffered in a fall, said he would do anything he could to pay full restitution of the stolen $10,060. But his attorney, Chuck Stidham, said Wilson's only income is $792 a month in Social Security and $80 a month for a sports column he still writes for the suburban newspaper.
Wilson's friends had contributed about $500 to a trust fund and may hold a charity event.
The judge said one beneficiary helped by the Christmas fund wrote with an offer to pay $20 a month to help the former editor pay off his debt.
Wilson began his newspaper career in Panama City, Florida, in 1938 and had been associated with the Valley Courier for about 40 years.
